summary.headline: WeWork India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28.5% YoY to INR698 crores and PAT reached INR53.2 crores (vs INR8.4 crores), with sequential dip from last quarter's customization one-off.
summary.overview: Management asked investors to judge the quarter year-on-year, not sequentially, because Q4 FY26 included about INR47 crores of one-time customization income versus INR9.5 crores this quarter. Revenue grew 28.5% YoY to INR698 crores, company EBITDA rose 69% to INR138.3 crores at a 19.8% margin, and occupancy reached 84.9%. Capex was INR188 crores in the quarter, FCFF was negative INR46 crores, and net debt fell to INR31.6 crores. Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth above 20% and capex guidance of INR500-600 crores, and it changed the accounting treatment for large managed-office customization.

segments.name: Core workspace
segments.commentary: INR603 crores in Q1 FY27, up 30% YoY and 3.4% QoQ; the largest revenue line.

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: Grew 10% YoY; includes parking, facilities, customization and late fees. Customization fell to INR9.5 crores from about INR47 crores in Q4 FY26, and VAS ex-customization grew about 20% QoQ.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: INR26 crores, up 27% YoY and 22% QoQ; management says it runs at close to 80% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Rivet and Member Services (new)
segments.commentary: Rivet is at a nascent stage with no major revenue booked in Q1; management guides 10-15% margin. Member Services was launched 15 July 2026 with take rates of about 6-16% plus listing fees.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth guided at over 20%; management says it is 'very confident' of this even as expansion rolls out.
Company EBITDA margin expected at 19-20% and rising through the year; Q2 margin expected to move up, not dip, on a YoY and QoQ basis.
Capex guidance of INR500-600 crores for the year held; may change if large managed-office deals need extra capex, with clarity expected by next quarter.
Operating capacity targeted at about 10.3 million sq ft and about 155,000 desks by March 2027; about 12 million sq ft by FY28 per management.
Customization revenue run-rate expected at INR10-15 crores per quarter; large single-client managed-office customization will be amortised over the member contract term.
VAS plus digital expected at 13-16% of revenue (VAS 11-12%, digital 3-4%).
capex_capacity: Operational: 79 centers across eight cities, 9.1 million sq ft and about 133.6 thousand desks, up 11 centers and nearly 20,000 desks YoY.
Contracted pipeline: signed leases and LOIs add 2.9 million sq ft, taking total contracted capacity to about 12 million sq ft and about 179,000 desks; about 44,000 desks already locked in.

Around 20,000 seats to open between Q1 and October 2026, including about 6,000 managed-office desks already signed; about 6,000 desks opened in the first 15 days of July; Q2 openings of about 15,000 seats, with about 7,000 managed-office seats.
H1 FY27 additions on track for about 22,000 desks; FY28 and FY29 supply is in negotiation, with visibility of about 12 months at 100%, 18 months at about 90% and 24 months at about 80%.
Rent per sq ft flat YoY; opex per sq ft up 5.6%; portfolio break-even occupancy 56.6%; revenue-to-rent ratio held at 2.9-3x.
demand_pricing: Portfolio occupancy 84.9% vs 76.5% a year ago; mature centers 87.5%; growth centers (under 12 months old) 65% vs 45% a year ago; members about 113,000, up 26,000 (about 30%) YoY.
Desk sales about 12,700 in Q1, up 28% YoY; April was the biggest sales month at about 7,500 desks, with no discounting; 52% of desk sales came from existing members; renewal rate 84%.
Revenue mix: 77% from enterprise members, 65% from global companies, North America 46% of revenue, technology 28%, BFSI 17%; top 10 members 22% of revenue.

Contracted future revenue INR3,363 crores, up 60% YoY from INR2,105 crores; committed rent rose about INR200 crores, so contracted revenue grows about 2x faster than contracted cost. Average remaining term about 27 months.
Pricing: Aerocity (Delhi) desks at INR25,000-35,000 per desk; southern markets priced about half that with spreads of 2.8-3x or higher.
Market: Q2 CY26 flex-space leasing led the market; flex is 27% of all office leasing and about 55% of occupiers use flex.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be one-time customization revenue from the 15,000-16,000 seats opening this quarter, and how fast do new seats reach EBITDA break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 20,000 seats open by October and all cohorts are already profitable. Customization will be recognised over the contract term for large managed-office work, with a run-rate of INR10-15 crores a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR500-600 crore capex guidance being kept?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, guidance is held; any change depends on large managed-office deals, with visibility by the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 margins dip YoY or QoQ given heavy openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect a dip. Margin is seen moving up because about 7,000 managed-office seats open in Q2, and management points to a 19-20% margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ growth guidance intact on a quarterly basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth above 20%, citing about 70% YoY EBITDA growth; it expects EBITDA to rise each quarter from the Rs138 crore base.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in mature and growth-cohort occupancy and the seat exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mature-cohort capacity rose about 8,000 seats as a result of cohort migration. Growth-cohort occupancy fell from 73% to 65% because about 7,000 new seats opened, and mature-cohort EBITDA margin is holding at about 28%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the managed-office customization model work and could REITs compete?
qa_highlights.answer: Customization is billed upfront when clients ask for changes beyond the contract price and is now amortised over the term. Management argues clients prefer one operator across formats, and REITs typically require longer commitments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Rivet and Member Services economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Rivet is a 10-15% margin business with direct flow-through to PAT and no capex. Member Services take rates are 6-16% plus listing fees, and some services will be booked as margin rather than revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the promoter share pledge?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% of shares are pledged against roughly INR570 crores of residual debt; about 30 lakh shares release next quarter, and the goal is to clear the pledge in FY27 via asset sales or a block deal.

risks_watch: Lumpiness of customization income and its amortisation under the new treatment; the Q1 sequential dip in EBITDA and PAT is driven by the Q4 one-off.
Growth-cohort occupancy fell to 65% from 73% QoQ as about 7,000 new seats opened; ramp-up of around 20,000 seats by October is the key execution risk.
Capex may move above INR500-600 crores if large managed-office deals require it.
Promoter pledge of about 15% of shares (INR570 crore debt residual) remains to be cleared.
Renewal and refurbishment cost of managed-office sites at year 6-7, plus the cash/P&L gap from brokerage amortisation.
Rivet is nascent with no major revenue in Q1; Member Services is newly launched on 15 July 2026 and its contribution is unproven.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on year-on-year growth, with defensive framing of the sequential decline as one-time customization timing. Management was specific on capacity, occupancy and contracted revenue, but it was less precise on the Q2 margin path and the reasons for the mature-cohort occupancy dip.
key_quotes: Look at us on a year-over-year basis, not sequentially, for two reasons.
This is not a warning sign, it is a model working as it is designed.

So, this will now from this year onwards actually smoothen out any type of lumpiness that we basically saw last year, and you'll have a more recurring base of customization revenue as the quarter's kind of flow through.
We don't foresee the margin dipping; we actually see potentially the margin moving upwards because of the large managed offices that are a component of that expansion coming up in Q2.

So, I think we 100% feel very confident that, you know, even as the expansion rolls out and the year rolls out, we will definitely meet the guidance of 20% plus EBITDA growth and sort of earnings sorry, revenue and EBITDA growth of, you know, over 20%.
